facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI (Registo Civil Integrado), introduced in 2023, is a web-based civil registration system with a centralised database, interconnected between the CR posts that use it and with the civil and criminal identification database.

The World Bank diagnostic states that births are registered in the RCI system from 2023 at civil registration posts, which issue a birth registration bulletin carrying the Unified Citizen Number; it describes no death registration in RCI.

The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI, first piloted in four Luanda registries, is available in all CR posts in Luanda and in one CR post each in Huambo, Benguela and Lubango, with plans to extend it gradually to the whole country; it gives no count of RCI offices, and elsewhere puts Luanda province at 39 CR units and the country at at least 255 CR units in 2023 (DNIRN data). No date is given for the coverage; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights (MINJUSDH) developed RCI, the new civil registration information system integrated with the identity card issuance system, introduced in 2023; its directorate DNIRN runs civil registration.
The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI was introduced in 2023, moved from a four-registry pilot in Luanda to all of Luanda's civil registry and is being gradually expanded to other provinces.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is a web-based civil registration system with no central database and no connection between the CR units using it, each unit holding its own infrastructure and data. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is used for civil registration and the issue of its documents, birth certificates included, and that computerised units issue a birth registration bulletin; it describes no death registration in SIRC. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that only the CR offices in Luanda, the provincial capitals and some municipalities, about half of the maternity clinic posts and the mobile registration kits are computerised, with registration equipment rolled out in Luanda, all provincial capitals and 34 maternity wards; it gives no count of computerised offices against the at least 255 CR units of 2023. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is maintained on request by MINJUSDH's Information and Communications Technology Cabinet or its provincial delegations, and that there is a vendor lock-in, the source code never having been given to the government. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that the Programme for the Modernization, Simplification and Computerization of Registry and Notary Services was launched in 2006 (Council of Ministers Resolution 39/06 of 17 July 2006) to computerise all civil registration and notary offices, a software contract followed in 2008 and SIRC was then rolled out in Luanda and the provincial capitals.

The World Bank diagnostic states that computerised registration posts in maternity clinics and mobile registration kits hold their data locally, the staff member copying it to an external disk, typically every six months, for upload to the SIRC database in the CR office. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that the majority of civil registration units still rely on paper-based records and that birth registration remains primarily paper-based, with most offices concentrated in urban centres; its example is Bembe municipality in Uíge, served by one non-computerised registration service. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that when a birth is registered at a rural CR post or health facility the pre-registration document must be forwarded to the appropriate CR office, which processes the certificate and records the information in paper ledgers or in a database. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that PROMOREN, a web-based civil registration system with a centralised database and biometric capture, used in two interconnected CR offices in Luanda and in the mobile units of the Massification project, is no longer used, the developer's technical assistance having been discontinued. The withdrawal is undated; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.
